analysis: The change is documentation-only in docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (head lines 451-488 added). It describes a selected-model recovery loop (ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery.swift) that retries operator-selected models skipped for memory. It uses allowEviction:false and evicts only idle, unprotected, non-excluded resident models that have met dwell and lease rules. No code, wire protocol, key custody, attestation, App Attest, cache-storage or coordinator-trust behavior changes in the supplied evidence. I checked the described behavior against the threat model. T-029 and A-018 (availability and idle timeout) are the closest fits. The described design includes guards against eviction loops and thrashing, and honors holds and exclusions, so TB-012/T-059 hold semantics appear consistent with the text. T-041 and the prefix-cache storage boundary are not touched. The patch excerpt is truncated at the end of the new paragraph, and the base units shown are unchanged surrounding text, so the full head text and the real implementation are not visible. Integration questions for any later pass: the actual SelectedModelRecovery code must be checked to confirm it respects the add-on hold (TB-012) and the load-transition gate, and that the recovery load path does not bypass the memory admission gates (evictUntilAvailable, KV headroom probe) or App Attest/serving authorization (TB-011) for newly loaded models. Those claims are unverified because no source was supplied. No security regression can be established from this documentation change alone.
